How we choose

Every place is recommended by named sources (review-aggregator star ratings never count as the recommender), pinned to its door from a published coordinate, and status-checked. Closed places stay, flagged, so you know they’re gone.

Must see
The places to plan a visit around — graded within each area, not across the city.
Worth the detour
Strong picks, worth going out of your way for.
Deep cut
For the curious: smaller, odder, more local.

Within each area, places are ordered by tier, then by number of named sources — never by popularity. Numbers on the cards match the pins on the map. No ratings, prices or opening hours are shown, because the guide doesn’t hold verified ones.

165 sights and 198 places to eat from Old City out to the Main Line, Camden and the Brandywine Valley, each traceable to the source that named it. Independence Hall, the Liberty Bell and the Art Museum steps anchor the map; the food runs on what Philadelphia is famous for — the cheesesteak and the roast pork Italian, the hoagie, tomato pie, soft pretzels, water ice and scrapple, Reading Terminal and the Italian Market, the Mexican and Vietnamese kitchens of South Philly, and a Michelin and James Beard bench.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Discovery started from what Philadelphia is famous for: the cheesesteak (measured — the famous Pat’s/Geno’s rivalry versus the locals’ and critics’ picks), the roast pork Italian, the hoagie, tomato pie, soft pretzels, water ice, scrapple and Tastykake; then Reading Terminal Market, the Italian Market, the Mexican kitchens of South 9th Street, the Vietnamese and Cambodian kitchens of Washington Ave and South Philly, and the Michelin and James Beard bench. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve; gaps are stated, not padded.

Web-searched, merit-measured and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, James Beard, the Philadelphia Inquirer, Philadelphia Magazine, Eater Philly, The Infatuation, Billy Penn / WHYY, Visit Philadelphia, the National Park Service, Atlas Obscura and vetted creators — recorded in data/sources.json (direct map/page fetches are blocked in the build environment, so sources were confirmed via search). A mention is not merit: each place needs two credible sources (or one Michelin / James Beard / NPS designation), and Yelp / TripAdvisor / Google count for nothing. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open or flagged CLOSED.
